SYNTHETIC – NOT A REAL PATIENT
HPI: The patient reports onset of low back pain on 02/22/2025. She reports pain radiating down one leg with no objective findings. She denies any red-flag symptoms such as trauma, cancer, fever, weight loss, bladder or bowel dysfunction, saddle anesthesia, or progressive neurologic deficit.
Exam: Lower-extremity strength, reflexes and sensation are normal.
Assessment: Lumbar radiculopathy without neurologic deficit.
Plan: Initiate NSAIDs today. Arrange physical therapy to start in one week. Return in 2 weeks.

SYNTHETIC – NOT A REAL PATIENT
HPI: The patient returns for follow‑up after completing a course of NSAIDs and physical therapy. NSAIDs were started on 02/23/2025 and discontinued on 04/05/2025 with a partial response. Physical therapy was begun on 03/01/2025, consisting of 10 sessions, and concluded on 04/05/2025 with no improvement. She continues to report pain radiating down one leg with no objective findings. She denies any red-flag symptoms such as trauma, cancer, fever, weight loss, bladder or bowel dysfunction, saddle anesthesia, or progressive neurologic deficit.
Exam: Lower-extremity strength, reflexes and sensation remain normal.
Assessment: Persistent lumbar radiculopathy, inadequate response to conservative measures.
Plan: Continue current analgesics as needed. Order lumbar MRI to further evaluate etiology.

SYNTHETIC – NOT A REAL PATIENT
HPI: The patient reports ongoing low back pain with radiculopathy despite completing NSAIDs and physical therapy. NSAIDs were started on 02/23/2025 and discontinued on 04/05/2025 with a partial response. Physical therapy was begun on 03/01/2025, consisting of 10 sessions, and concluded on 04/05/2025 with no improvement. She continues to describe pain radiating down one leg with no objective findings. She denies any red-flag symptoms such as trauma, cancer, fever, weight loss, bladder or bowel dysfunction, saddle anesthesia, or progressive neurologic deficit.
Exam: Lower-extremity strength, reflexes and sensation are normal.
Assessment: Chronic lumbar radiculopathy refractory to conservative therapy.
Plan: Obtain lumbar MRI to delineate anatomic correlates; epidural steroid injection or surgical referral will be considered based on results.
